segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: WE HAD A MONTH until Asura Kingdom sent word that its king had fallen ill. In that time, I had to work with Ariel to convince Perugius to join her side. To that end, I needed to pump Sylphie for all the details I could. But she probably had her guard up thanks to Orsted’s curse, so I might not be able to persuade her to bring me into Ariel’s plans. I was torn about whether to trust her and tell her the whole truth, or to give up fighting Orsted’s curse and avoid mentioning him altogether.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: But first, I had another objective to complete. Namely, the very reason why I’d agreed to work under Orsted to begin with—so I could protect my family. Now that I was his little errand boy, I’d be away from home more often. I needed someone—or something—to take my place.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Thus, my first order of business was summoning this Guardian Beast.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: It was still morning when I gathered all the members of my household in the garden. That included Aisha, Lilia, and Zenith, who normally spent all their time inside, as well as Eris, who had newly joined the family. Roxy and Norn were present too, as were Dillo and Byt. Sylphie carried Lucie, who had just recently learned to stand while holding onto something.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: In a moment, I will be summoning the Guardian Beast that will serve our family. Feel free to clap.

segments.speaker: Crowd
segments.text: Yay!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Applause rang from the crowd. The audience’s fervor was hitting its peak. Tonight’s concert would be legendary!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Hold up, Dillo and Byt. Why aren’t the two of you clapping? This just won’t do. What? They’re pets so they can’t clap? Well, I suppose it can’t be helped.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: As for exactly what I will be summoning, I am afraid I don’t know for sure. However, we can expect something particularly powerful. And this creature, whatever it is, will keep our family safe and secure.

segments.speaker: Sylphiette
segments.text: Are you sure this will be okay? That this thing won’t eat us all while you’re gone?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Sylphie asked, worried.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That’s a terrifying thought.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That said, I did recall reading a story like that a long time ago. Something about someone calling forth a beast they couldn’t control and it killing everyone.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I get you’re worried, but this was made by the meticulous hand of the Dragon God.

segments.speaker: Sylphiette
segments.text: Which is precisely why I’m worried.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Logically speaking, Orsted would never use such a roundabout way to get rid of us, but Sylphie probably wasn’t thinking straight thanks to his curse.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: But wait, could this be his way of putting a leash on me in case I betray him? Like, if I turn my back on him, will he threaten me?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: With a snap of my fingers, that beast residing at your house will devour your entire family.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That really didn’t seem likely.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: In any case, I’m going to summon it now. If it seems dangerous, we’ll get rid of it together, and then I can give Orsted an earful.

segments.speaker: Eris
segments.text: Sounds good to me!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Eris declared in excitement. She pulled a sword from its scabbard with a majestic clang. She had two at her hip. On the right was Eminence, a magic blade the Sword God had gifted her. On her left was one she had grown attached to and used for a long time.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Isn’t it cumbersome, carrying both at the same time?

segments.speaker: Eris
segments.text: When that happens, all of us will be able to fight Orsted together!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: she declared.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: We’re not going to fight. We’re just going to file a complaint, like a normal dissatisfied customer. If we tried to take him down, we’d be the ones kicking the bucket instead.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That said, she looked awfully happy. She wasn’t just looking for an excuse to pick a fight with him, was she?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: We won’t be fighting Orsted,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I said.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: But we’ll have plenty of chances to fight together in the future. I hope you’ll save your strength until then.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Her face sank, as if the idea bored her. It was fine if she wanted to fight other people, but Orsted was off limits. Never in my life did I want to fight another battle that hopeless if I could help it. I’d pee myself if I had to do it a second time.

segments.speaker: Roxy
segments.text: Still, are you really sure this magic circle is safe? Perhaps it might be a good idea to have someone like Lord Perugius look at it first?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: said Roxy. Apparently, she was also leery of something Orsted had made.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That curse on him really is powerful.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: As absurd as the whole curse nonsense seemed, the intensity of their reactions made its existence impossible to deny. That made my decision an easy one, though I did decide to take a second look at the scroll before I used it. I wouldn’t go so far as to have Perugius check it, but it couldn’t hurt to examine it once more myself.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Hm.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: It seemed like a normal summoning circle. The part that restricted the conditions of the summoning had some symbols I wasn’t familiar with, but there was nothing too suspicious, as far as I could tell. Perhaps I could have Nanahoshi take a look? No, that would be rude. Orsted only made this for me because I didn’t know how to do it myself. What good did it do to be this distrustful?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I’m sure it’s fine,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I said.

segments.speaker: Roxy
segments.text: Well, if you say so. I believe you. But wait just a second while I get my staff.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Roxy, it seemed, was not entirely convinced. She said she trusted me, but still disappeared inside the house to retrieve her weapon in case things got ugly.

segments.speaker: Norn
segments.text: I have no idea why everyone seems so on guard, but…you’re sure this isn’t dangerous, Big Brother?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Norn furrowed her brow.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Aisha clapped a hand on Norn’s shoulder.

segments.speaker: Aisha
segments.text: Don’t be stupid. If it were that dangerous, he wouldn’t activate it with us around.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Her trust felt like a dagger to the heart. Honestly, I hadn’t confirmed if this summoning circle was safe. Could I really just use it like this? Perhaps I should wait until I could get Perugius to check it, just to be sure?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: But if I did, Aisha’s affectionate gaze would turn to disappointment. And she’d only be suspicious of Orsted, after that.

segments.speaker: Lilia
segments.text: Should the worst come to pass, I will act as a shield for everyone. Please, do what you need,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: said Lilia.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Well, that sounds ominous.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I didn’t think it would come to that, but everyone else was so jumpy that I was on edge. Were we really going to be okay?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: No! I need to have faith in Orsted. He said he trusted me.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: All right then,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I said.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I’m going to use it.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Everyone nodded.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I set the scroll down on a table I’d erected using my earth magic.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Here goes.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I steeled myself and placed my hands on the circle. I concentrated, letting the magic flow through my veins and gather in my fingertips. From there, I poured it into the circle.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I kept pumping more and more of my mana in. This creature was supposed to be something that could protect my family. Even if I drained myself dry, it still wouldn’t be enough in my eyes. I’d gladly take every last bit of Orsted’s mana too, if I could. Using more mana didn’t necessarily guarantee a strong Guardian Beast, but I would still give this everything I had.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Orsted also said it was important to imagine what I wanted.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Something to protect my family…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That was awfully vague.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I needed something incredibly powerful. Powerful enough that a normal opponent wouldn’t stand a chance. Something that was incredibly loyal and would never oppose me. And since they were supposed to be protecting my family, preferably not something crude and indecent. I definitely didn’t want some tentacle monster covered in mucus. That wouldn’t be good for my little sisters or Lucie. This Guardian Beast was going to be Lucie’s knight, so I needed something respectable.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That’s right. A creature of high moral character, who is loyal and strong. Okay, order up, let’s go!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Come on out, Guardian Beast!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The circle began emitting a bright light, not a pure white but a mix of blue, red, yellow, and green. It was a whole rainbow. But I felt as if the summoning had caught on something—as if there was something stopping it.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: What could it be?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I ignored it and continued pouring in more mana. Whatever had been blocking the spell snapped.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: Aaaah!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: A voice groaned, though I couldn’t tell where the sound came from. Was it the Guardian Beast that would now be protecting my family? It sounded rather ominous, as if the creature was in pain. I simply increased my mana output, yanking whatever it was through the summoning circle.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: Aaaaah!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: A voice rang out as the mana flow I’d been feeding into the circle was abruptly cut off.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The light faded, and from within it appeared…

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: Khh…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: A man in a yellow mask and white uniform, a large dagger hanging by his side. He was perched atop the earthen platform I had created, down on one knee with his arms wrapped around himself.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: How can this be… How could my contract with Lord Perugius be destroyed like this…?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: He remained in that pose as he lifted his head and looked around. The mask obscured his eyes, but I could swear he was staring straight at me.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: What’s the meaning of this?!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: the masked man demanded.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: No, it was wrong to call him that. I knew exactly who this was.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Arumanfi the Bright.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The way he’s posed reminds me of a fallen angel. Not that I’m trying to make light of him, I swear. I’d never be able to hold a candle to his brightness. He’s way more lit than I am. Just kidd—

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: I asked you, Rudeus Greyrat, what your intention is here?!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: He leapt from the table and tried to seize me by the collar, only to freeze midway through, his entire body trembling.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Eris immediately moved into battle stance, but I held a hand up to stay her.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Bad girl. Go to your pen, Eris.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Seriously, what was going on? I had summoned the bright and noble Arumanfi, of all people. Was that even possible? Although—despite his human form, he was actually a spirit. Perhaps this wasn’t so surprising, after all. Not that that explained everything. Was this all a ploy by Orsted? Was he trying to provoke Perugius, to get him to kill me instead?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Oh, come on, if you’re going to go that far, then just do the job yourself.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Uh, no, you see… This just kinda happened… I was activating a magic circle that Sir Orsted gave me, and it sort of…summoned you here by accident.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: Orsted’s magic circle, you say? What precisely were you trying to summon?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: A Guardian Beast to watch over my family.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Arumanfi snatched up the scroll with the magic circle. He studied it before gaping.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: These are some bothersome stipulations he’s placed on the summoned entity…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Um, what conditions are they?

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: The one this circle summons must be absolutely obedient to you, and they are to defend your family against any calamities that might befall them in perpetuity. In other words, they are to serve for eternity.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Wow. So this magic circle was basically a slave contract?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Well, the good news is that Orsted didn’t lie to me. Looks like he’s trustworthy after all!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Anything else?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I asked.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: The summoner will be the one who determines precisely what is called forth.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: So basically, I could decide what Guardian Beast I received. Great.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Then I’d like to make an exchange.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: An exchange?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Yes, I didn’t mean to summon you, Mister Arumanfi. So I’d like to trade you out for someone else.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: Then hurry up and dissolve your contract with me. I am Lord Perugius’s proud servant, not yours.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Uh, yeah. Right.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Honestly, it wasn’t a terrible idea having Arumanfi to protect our family. He moved at the speed of light, so if anything unforeseen happened, he’d be the perfect person to relay a message to me.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Yeah, but Perugius values him too much. If I took him away, it might cause discord between us.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I furrowed my brow.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Um, so how do I go about doing that, exactly?

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: Order me to return to Lord Perugius’s side immediately. Dotbath of Destruction will be able to sever the contract.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: All right.

segments.speaker: Arumanfi
segments.text: Order me. Now.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Due to the absolute obedience clause, he needed a direct order from me to leave.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Okay, then by the power of this summoning circle, I command you to go to Lord Perugius and request advice from him as to how best to call forth a good Guardian Beast.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Arumanfi kept the magic circle in his hands as he disappeared in a flash of light.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Sorry everyone, looks like I screwed up,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I said as I glanced back at my family.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: They were all staring at me, slack-jawed.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Arumanfi returned after a while. He delivered a message from Perugius before, hissing about how he’d let this transgression slide but it had better never happen again. Arumanfi was extremely proud of his status as Perugius’s servant, after all. I did feel genuinely guilty about stealing that from him, however temporarily.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The circle that Orsted had drawn me apparently lost its power when the contract was annulled, so Perugius made me a new one. It was hard to believe he’d show me such kindness after I so rudely swiped one of his servants. He really was as magnanimous as Sylvaril claimed.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The truly terrifying part of the whole ordeal was the level of power Orsted’s circle had commanded. Or maybe it was my own magic that was to blame? Perhaps both. Each was merely a spark on its own, but combined, they made a raging flame.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Since the previous summoning hadn’t depleted much of my mana, I decided to collect myself and try again immediately. According to Perugius, it was better not to imagine vague concepts like majestic, omniscient, or omnipotent, but rather, an animal.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: If that was all, I wish Orsted had simply said so. But knowing him, he’d probably have told me to keep Arumanfi, as crazy as that idea sounded.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Okay, let’s try this again.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I surveyed the area before putting my hands on the magic circle once more. This time, I was going to keep a concrete image in my mind. I wanted a strong, proud animal.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: A lion!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I had no idea if they existed here as I knew them, but the word existed in the language, so surely there was something similar. I wanted the king of beasts—the strongest creature this world had to offer. Although, if I wanted something loyal, I might be better served by a canine, rather than a feline.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Nah, that doesn’t matter. The magic circle requires absolute obedience, so I just need to focus on something that’s strong. I want the most noble beast that exists in this world.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I focused all the magic I had in every corner of my body into my right hand. For a few moments, I squeezed my eyes shut, but as the last drops of mana left my body and poured into the circle, I snapped them open again.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Come on! Bring home the bacon!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I sucked in a breath as the magic circle emitted a dazzling light. It was the same colorful rainbow I had seen earlier, but this time, I didn’t experience the sensation of the spell snagging on something. My mana flowed smoothly into the circle, and whatever was on the other end heeded my call. In fact, it felt as though a hand was being extended toward me, and all I had to do was take it and pull. I was confident that I would be successful this time.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: All right, come on out!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I hollered.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: A faint howl echoed through the air.

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Awoooo!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: It grew louder and louder, ringing in my ears.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Is there something I should be saying right now as I’m summoning this thing? I guess it doesn’t matter…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: As I debated that, the light disappeared. What stood before me was a white lion, over two meters tall. I assumed it was female since it had no mane. The way its snout extended, however, reminded me more of a dog than a cat.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Wait, this is no lion. It’s a dog. And judging by how short its legs are, it’s a pup at that.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: In fact, upon closer inspection, I realized its fur wasn’t white, but silver. It looked like a baby Shiba Inu, but far more massive.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Hmm… Did I botch it again?

segments.speaker: Aisha
segments.text: It’s adorable!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Aisha exclaimed.

segments.speaker: Norn
segments.text: But do you really think this thing can protect us?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Norn frowned.

segments.speaker: Sylphiette
segments.text: Well,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: said Sylphie,

segments.speaker: Sylphiette
segments.text: for a pup, it does look confident.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Roxy nodded.

segments.speaker: Roxy
segments.text: At the very least, it looks too innocent for anyone to suspect it’s a Guardian Beast.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The two of them seemed approving enough.

segments.speaker: Lilia
segments.text: It does look intelligent,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Lilia commented. She had a perfect poker face so it was hard to tell what she was thinking, but she wasn’t knitting her brows or frowning at least.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Zenith was expressionless as ever. I had no idea what Byt thought of our newest addition, but Dillo was already on his back, expressing submission toward our Guardian Beast.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Not too bad as far as first impressions went.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Although, I’m pretty sure I’ve seen this pup before.

segments.speaker: Eris
segments.text: Hold on,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: said Eris.

segments.speaker: Eris
segments.text: Isn’t this the Sacred Beast that was so attached to you back in Doldia Village, Rudeus?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That’s right! I just remembered. Uh, what were the words in Beast God Tongue again…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I cleared my throat and said,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Are you perhaps the Sacred Beast from Doldia?

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Woof.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The great dog bobbed its head in response before licking my face.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Ugh, it stinks. Dammit, what does this thing take me for? A piece of meat?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: At least I finally knew exactly what I had summoned.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I see.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The Sacred Beast, huh? The same one the Doldia tribe treasured so much that they locked it away deep within their village…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Crap. If they found out that I summoned it to serve as my personal guardian, they would be absolutely livid, wouldn’t they? If they put me on their wanted list, it would only cause more problems. I already had enough on my plate.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Guess I gotta exchange this one too…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Although annulling the contract would cause more trouble for either Perugius or Orsted. And there was no guarantee I’d get anything better on the third try.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Hmm…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I spoke in Beast God Tongue.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: O Sacred Beast, if I might humbly ask, do you possess the power to protect my family from any calamity that might befall them?

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Woof!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: He seemed to be saying,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Leave everything to me!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: He seemed motivated enough, but on the other hand, he had gotten himself kidnapped before. Could I really rely on him to protect them? Orsted assured me that the Man-God probably wouldn’t come after my family much anymore, so maybe I didn’t have anything to worry about, but…

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Arf?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: As I was lost in thought, the Sacred Beast leaped from the summoning table and pressed its body against me, licking at my face again.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Ahh, he’s so soft… They definitely have to be using some kinda conditioner on him. And if he’s our Guardian Beast, that means I’ll be able to enjoy his fluffy fur every single day.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Yep, I’ve gotta be mistaken. This definitely isn’t the Sacred Beast.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Nope. This was not the holy creature the beastfolk looked up to with such reverence. Definitely not. There was no way their protector god would show up here of all places. It had to be a look-alike.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: That’s right. This thing is a…a lion, that’s it!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: It was clearly a lion cub I had called here from one of an infinite number of alternate worlds. At least, that was the explanation I decided upon in my mind. It was good enough for me. Although that excuse probably wouldn’t hold water when it came to protecting me from the wrath of the Doldia.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Well, if things started going sideways, I could always ask Lord Perugius for a favor and swap this lion cub for something else. Until then, we’d have a trial period of sorts.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: All right. From today forth, your name is Leo!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I proclaimed, thrusting my hand into the air.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: The Sacred Beast promptly licked my fingers before snorting in response. Then, suddenly, he lifted his head as if he had noticed something. His gaze turned toward Roxy. Leo trotted over to her before promptly shoving his face up her skirt.

segments.speaker: Roxy
segments.text: Ack! Hey! What are you doing?!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Roxy cried, bonking him with her staff.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Our perverted canine merely sniffed and licked at her leg before wrapping his enormous body around her.

segments.speaker: Roxy
segments.text: Um, Rudy… What am I supposed to do about this?

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Nervously, she peered over at me.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I had no idea what was going on exactly, but it was clear that our new family member was attached to Roxy.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Leo, now that I have summoned you here, you’re my servant,

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I said in Beast God Tongue.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Your duty is to protect my family. Understood?

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Woof!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: he barked back cheerfully.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I had no idea how useful a pup would be for watching over everyone, but since this was what I had summoned, it was going to be our Guardian Beast henceforth.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Surely, he’ll prove his worth.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Leo, allow me to explain a bit about what your employment here entails. I know you’re used to getting your way and having people spoil you, but that won’t fly here. You’re going to have to wear a collar and live in a dog house like a normal canine. If anyone suspicious appears, you bark at them, bite them, and render them powerless. If they’re too strong, you have my permission to kill them. You’ll have three meals a day here, and you’re free to take naps whenever you want. If you so desire, we’ll even take you for walks when you want. If you find these conditions acceptable, please bark once.

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Woof!

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Great, that’s the kind of answer I like to hear. And one more thing…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: It goes without saying that if you dare do anything to hurt my family…

segments.speaker: Leo
segments.text: Arf…

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: His throat rumbled, as if he were offended by the mere idea.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: Great. Then our contract is sealed. Now let’s shake on it.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: I held out my hand and he promptly offered up his paw.

segments.speaker: Rudeus
segments.text: And with that, our family had a new pet.
